final.title: Shared logins hide the access record problem
final.body:
Shared logins are usually a convenience choice, not a strategy. For a small business, the real issue is not the password itself. It is the missing access record: who has the login, who gave it to them, and when access should end.

That matters because once a shared account is used for day-to-day work, you lose the trail. If something gets changed or deleted, it takes longer to work out what happened. If someone leaves, you may also be left guessing which accounts still open the door. That is a general workflow risk, not a dramatic one. It just sits there until you need it.

The practical next step is simple: ask one question inside the business — who has access to our shared accounts, who added them, and when will they lose it? If nobody can answer that cleanly, the problem is already visible.

From there, you can decide whether the fix is manual documentation, password management, or a more formal access process. The point is to make the decision bounded before it turns into cleanup. Shared logins work until they do not, and small teams usually notice at the least convenient moment.
